title: The mountains that aren't done yet

concepts.label: Frost Wedging
concepts.what: Freeze-thaw weathering: water in rock cracks expands ~9% on freezing, progressively fracturing rock; dominant weathering process at Himalayan altitudes.

concepts.label: Fold Mountains
concepts.what: Mountains formed at convergent plate boundaries by compressional forces folding and thrusting crustal layers upward; Earth's highest ranges are fold mountains.

concepts.label: Alpine-Himalayan Belt
concepts.what: Continuous mountain arc from Atlas Mountains (Morocco) through Alps, Caucasus, Zagros, Hindu Kush, Karakoram, Himalayas, bending south as Burmese arc into Indonesia.

concepts.label: American Cordilleras
concepts.what: North-to-south mountain arc: Rockies (North America) + Andes (South America); formed by subduction along Pacific margin; world's longest continuous mountain chain.

concepts.label: East Asian Island Arcs
concepts.what: Pacific island arc system (Japan, Philippines, western Pacific); formed by oceanic-plate subduction under Asian margin, not continent-continent collision.

concepts.label: Himalayas
concepts.what: Young fold mountain system running 2,400 km from Indus gorge (west) to Brahmaputra gorge (east); three to four parallel ridges stacked south to north; still tectonically active.

concepts.label: Trans-Himalayas
concepts.what: Northernmost Himalayan zone (Karakoram, Ladakh ranges); absolute altitude peaks here (K2: 8,611 m); largest glacial ice mass in the system; inner side of India-Eurasia collision.

concepts.label: Greater Himalayas (Himadri)
concepts.what: Main Himalayan watershed; crests rarely below 6,000 m; permanently snow-covered; holds all 8,000+ m peaks; composed of ancient upthrust Indian basement granite.

concepts.label: Sagarmatha (Everest)
concepts.what: World's highest peak at 8,849 m in Nepal Himalayas; also called Everest (English) and Chomolungma (Tibetan); part of Greater Himalayas.

concepts.label: Kanchenjunga
concepts.what: World's third-highest peak at 8,586 m; at Nepal-Sikkim junction; marks transition to wetter, narrower eastern Himalayan section.

concepts.label: Nanda Devi
concepts.what: Highest summit entirely within India at 7,816 m; in Garhwal (Uttarakhand) Himalayas; within Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve.

concepts.label: Nanga Parbat (Western Syntaxis)
concepts.what: 8,126 m; western anchor of Greater Himalayas at the western syntaxis where the Himalayan arc bends sharply; known for vast south face relief.

concepts.label: Namcha Barwa (Eastern Syntaxis)
concepts.what: 7,782 m; eastern syntaxis point where Greater Himalayas bend abruptly south; beyond this the range continues north-south as Purvanchal.

concepts.label: Lesser Himalayas (Himachal)
concepts.what: Second Himalayan zone south of Greater Himalayas; 3,700–4,500 m average altitude; location of major hill stations and three examiner-tested sub-ranges.

concepts.label: Pir Panjal Range
concepts.what: Longest sub-range of Lesser Himalayas; runs through Jammu, Kashmir, and Himachal Pradesh; southern wall of the Kashmir Valley.

concepts.label: Dhauladhar Range
concepts.what: Sub-range of Lesser Himalayas through Himachal Pradesh; one of three examiner-tested Lesser Himalayan sub-ranges (Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mahabharat).

concepts.label: Mahabharat Range
concepts.what: Sub-range of Lesser Himalayas through Nepal; one of three examiner-tested Lesser Himalayan sub-ranges; separates inner and outer Himalayan Nepal.

concepts.label: Kashmir Valley
concepts.what: Intermontane basin cradled between Pir Panjal (south) and Greater Himalayas (north); ~130 km × 40 km; one of world's most celebrated high-altitude structural basins.

concepts.label: Main Central Thrust (MCT)
concepts.what: Major fault plane at the boundary between Greater and Lesser Himalayas; rock slabs thrust southward over each other; primary locus of Himalayan earthquakes.

concepts.label: Main Boundary Thrust (MBT)
concepts.what: Major fault plane between Lesser Himalayas and Shivaliks; marks the active collision frontier; associated with ongoing seismic activity.

concepts.label: Shivaliks (Outer Himalayas)
concepts.what: Outermost, youngest Himalayan range; 900–1,100 m; made of unconsolidated river sediment folded by the advancing collision front; still sweeping southward.

concepts.label: Duns (Longitudinal Valleys)
concepts.what: Flat-floored longitudinal valleys between Shivaliks and Lesser Himalayas; carved by erosion of softer rock between thrust ridges; Dehradun is the most famous example.

concepts.label: Himalayan Regional Sections (West to East)
concepts.what: Himalayan arc divided into regional sections: Punjab-Kashmir (widest, ~400 km, densely glaciated), Kumaon-Garhwal, Nepal (Sagarmatha), Sikkim-Darjeeling (narrow, wet), Arunachal (eastern syntaxis).

concepts.label: Purvanchal (Eastern Highlands)
concepts.what: Himalayan fold system reoriented north-south beyond eastern syntaxis; Patkai, Naga, Manipur, Mizo hills; same collision origin as Himalayas, different orientation.

concepts.label: Burmese Arc
concepts.what: Continuation of the Alpine-Himalayan fold system running south through Myanmar and Indonesia; begins where Purvanchal bends past the eastern syntaxis.

concepts.label: Tethys Marine Fossils at Altitude
concepts.what: Marine fossils (ammonites) at 4,000–5,000 m in Ladakh and Spiti; ancient Tethys sea-floor sediment compressed and uplifted during India-Eurasia collision; vivid proof of plate tectonics.

concepts.label: The Third Pole
concepts.what: Karakoram-Hindu Kush-Pamir-Himalaya cluster holds largest glacial ice mass outside Antarctica and Greenland; informally called the Third Pole; feeds major Asian river systems.

concepts.label: Siachen Glacier
concepts.what: ~76 km mountain glacier in Karakoram; among world's longest; source of Nubra river; holds strategic military significance (India-Pakistan).

concepts.label: Gangotri Glacier
concepts.what: Major glacier in Garhwal (Uttarakhand); primary source of Ganga river system; retreating under climate change; located within Gangotri National Park.

concepts.label: Himalayan Glacial Meltwater Dependency
concepts.what: Major rivers (Indus, Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra) depend on Himalayan glacial meltwater as a slow seasonal reservoir; agricultural calendars across Indo-Gangetic plains calibrated to melt rhythms.

concepts.label: Himalayan Seismic Hazard
concepts.what: Entire Himalayan front above active collision interface; Hindu Kush–Pamir knot among most seismically active zones globally; Bihar-Nepal 1934, Kashmir 2005, Nepal 2015 are landmark events.

concepts.label: Aravalli Range
concepts.what: Fold mountains (~800 km, near Delhi to Gujarat); among world's oldest — Precambrian, 2–3 billion years; Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) is highest point; heavily eroded over eons.
